_comment: Trap Map: Research-based thesis cards with falsification tests. Each trap corresponds to one research piece and tracks validation status. FORBIDDEN: any language about holdings, portfolio positions, share counts, powder, IRA, buy/sell sizing, or whether 'we' hold the name.

_field_definitions.id: Stable slug identifier for the trap (e.g., 'power-scarcity-trap-1')
_field_definitions.title: Short headline for the card
_field_definitions.thesis_summary: One-paragraph stranger-usable summary of the thesis
_field_definitions.who_collects_rent: Entity/mechanism that captures economic rent vs residual claimants
_field_definitions.validation_status: One of: WATCH (monitoring), HOLD (thesis intact, waiting), POUNCE (conditions met), RELEGATE (thesis falsified or obsolete)
_field_definitions.decisive_test: Single stranger-checkable test that validates or falsifies the thesis
_field_definitions.next_datapoint: Optional: { label, expected_date, source_hint } for automated tracking
_field_definitions.research_ref: Path or URL to the underlying research piece/memo
_field_definitions.sources: Array of { label, url, date } primary sources

traps.title: Power & Interconnect Scarcity
traps.thesis_summary: AI infrastructure buildout is bottlenecked by firm watts and cleared interconnection paths, not just GPU supply. Datacenters with power purchase agreements and grid-ready sites command premium valuations. The constraint timeline extends through 2027+ as hyperscalers race to secure capacity.
traps.who_collects_rent: Utilities with contracted generation capacity, landowners with transmission-ready sites, and datacenter developers with executed PPAs. GPU makers are price-takers at the power constraint; power providers are rent collectors.
traps.decisive_test: Track hyperscaler capex allocation: if >40% of disclosed AI capex goes to power/infrastructure vs compute hardware across major hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META) for 2 consecutive quarters, scarcity thesis is validated. If GPU supply normalizes and capex pivots back to hardware-first, thesis weakens.

traps.title: ASTS BlueBird Constellation Watch
traps.thesis_summary: AST SpaceMobile's thesis hinges on BlueBird satellite constellation achieving commercial service. Secondary offerings dilute existing shareholders but fund constellation buildout. The key validation is whether the technology delivers promised direct-to-cell coverage at scale.
traps.who_collects_rent: If successful, ASTS captures rent as infrastructure owner with spectrum partnerships. MNO partners (AT&T, Vodafone) share economics but ASTS holds the orbital assets. If constellation fails, capital is stranded.
traps.decisive_test: First 5 BlueBird satellites must demonstrate commercial-grade voice/data throughput to unmodified smartphones in partner MNO coverage gaps within 6 months of launch. Throughput <1 Mbps average or coverage gaps >50% of target zones falsifies thesis.

next_datapoint.label: BlueBird Launch & Early Ops
next_datapoint.source_hint: ASTS investor updates, FCC filings, partner MNO press releases

traps.title: ARKG Thesis Validation Framework
traps.thesis_summary: ARK Genomics (ARKG) represents a basket bet on multi-year genomic medicine timelines. The thesis validates not as a position but as a research framework: do ARK's core bets (CRISPR therapeutics, multi-omics diagnostics, synthetic biology) hit clinical/commercial milestones within stated timeframes?
traps.who_collects_rent: Platform companies with approved therapies and reimbursement pathways collect rent. Tools-only companies remain picks-and-shovels. ARKG as a vehicle takes management fees regardless of thesis accuracy.
traps.decisive_test: Track top 10 ARKG holdings by weight: if ≥4 achieve FDA approval or significant commercial revenue (>$500M annual) by end of 2027, innovation thesis validates. If <2 hit milestones and fund underperforms biotech benchmark by >20% cumulative, framework requires revision.

next_datapoint.source_hint: FDA PDUFA dates, company earnings, ARK monthly reports

traps.title: Buyback as Confession (Captive Duration)
traps.thesis_summary: When Treasury doubles long-end liquidity-support buybacks concurrent with 10s/30s issuance, the regime signals that private sponsorship of duration is insufficient without a structural state bid. This is the captive-buyer system around the bond, not a one-off support headline. The money is in who warehouses duration and the issuer as standing long-end bid.
traps.who_collects_rent: Whoever sets captivity/balance-sheet rules and runs the buyback backstop — regulators, Treasury, Fed plumbing. Dealers take warehouse/fees. Equity of stuffed franchises is residual.
traps.decisive_test: (1) 10y/30y auctions cover at/above recent averages with strong indirects → private bid intact, buyback expansion is cosmetic. (2) First enlarged long-end buyback ops undersubscribe vs claim of 'strong sponsorship' → plumbing story overstated. (3) QRA buyback max sizes cut back or framed as temporary → structural state-bid claim fails.

next_datapoint.source_hint: Treasury auction results, QRA announcement, Fed buyback operations
